claims.statement: The revised EU buildings framework is expected to increase workplace and building charging points and explicitly supports smart charging.
The EU alternative-fuels framework sets infrastructure targets and includes interoperability, payment, transparency, and smart-charging provisions for publicly available charging.

contrary_evidence: Rules that add charging points do not prove those points will have unused, transferable overnight capacity.
AFIR provisions for publicly available infrastructure may not govern a private reserved-access model in the same way.

economics.acquisition_route: Property managers, charging installers, fleet lessors, courier contractors, and geo-targeted direct sales
economics.founder_net_worth_path: A possible path is several thousand contracted ports across Polish cities, generating recurring access margin and a valuable two-sided network
economics.founder_time: Initially 12-20 hours per week, with physical support supplied by charging partners
economics.gross_margin_basis: Expected 30-50% after host share, access hardware, support, payment, and downtime credits
economics.payback: Unvalidated; approximately 100-200 occupied port-months may cover a lean pilot depending on integration cost
economics.pricing: Unvalidated: 500-1200 PLN per reserved port-month plus transparent energy and overage charges
economics.retention_or_repeat: Fleet routes and overnight needs recur monthly; host contracts should run two to five years

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Dense contracted time slots, route-demand data, host integrations, and backup coverage improve reliability and local liquidity
fingerprint.customer: Urban delivery, taxi, field-service, and light-commercial fleets without sufficient depot charging
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Acquire hosts through property managers and installers; acquire fleets through leasing firms, dispatch software, and local route-density analysis
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Guaranteed recurring windows, access control, smart scheduling, uptime monitoring, settlement, and backup-site routing
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The fleet pays a monthly per-port reservation and energy or utilization charge; hosts receive a contracted share
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A fleet electrifies vehicles but lacks guaranteed overnight charging near operating routes

founder_fit: Uses optimization, forecasting, and energy-sector access
Can start with existing hardware rather than funding charging stations
Warsaw provides a dense initial geography
risks: Electricity resale, parking, tax, and public-access rules may apply
Charger downtime can disrupt fleet operations and create claims
Hosts may withdraw access after fleets depend on it
Night operations could create safety and site-security issues

structure.control_point: Reserved recurring charging and parking windows at host-controlled sites
structure.critical_dependency: Host grid capacity, charger uptime, parking rights, and fleet-route demand must overlap reliably

thesis: Contract exclusive overnight scheduling rights at underused private workplace, hotel, retail, and industrial chargers, then sell delivery and service fleets guaranteed recurring charging and parking windows near their routes.
title: Guaranteed Overnight Fleet-Charging Slot Network
uncertainties: Unknown quantity of genuinely unused private overnight capacity
Unknown fleet willingness to rely on third-party sites
No host or fleet reservation price has been validated
Polish energy-resale and property-access structure needs legal review
